# Loment 0.1.4.6

Sixty-eight pull requests since `0.1.4.5-quickfix`. Three of them are things getting their first real
version — an interpreter tier beside the compiler, libc reachable from both sides of the link, and a
gate that can finally see the runtime it is supposed to guard. The rest is the largest defect sweep
this project has had; most of the issue numbers below come from it.

This is not an exhaustive changelog — the issue and pull-request numbers are the index.

## Install

| Asset | |
|---|---|
| `loment-0.1.4.6-linux-x64.tar.gz` | Linux x86-64. Unpack anywhere; `bin/loment` is the launcher. |
| `loment-0.1.4.6-windows-x64.zip` | Windows x86-64. Unzip and run `install.cmd`. |
| `loment-0.1.4.6-windows-x64-setup.exe` | Windows x86-64, self-extracting. Double-click. |
| `loment-skill.zip` | The agent guide (`SKILL.md`) on its own, for people who want only that. |
| `SHA256SUMS` | Checksums. The installers verify the payload against this before copying anything. |

Installing and running needs **no Python, no clang and no WSL** — the package is native binaries plus
the standard library.

## new

- **A second way to run a program: LVM.** The interpreter reads the same IR the linker does, so a
  program never gains a second source of truth. T0 was the fourth reader of that IR (#277); T1 records
  a feedback profile without changing a byte of output (#379); T2 moves instruction decoding out of the
  execution loop — **6.1× T0** on the corpus, byte-identical output (#587); #328's compact form is
  **375.9 KB → 107.0 KB** for the same unit (#588); T3 adds guarded specialisation and deoptimisation
  (#589). Specs: `docs/243`, `docs/247`, `docs/259`, `docs/250`, `docs/261`.
- **Threads.** `thread_spawn` in the language, plus an `os/thread` library whose syscall numbers are
  read from the header rather than remembered (#349, `docs/245`).
- **Four shipped libraries, each judged against a real implementation.** `os` — 5 modules against
  CPython in the same Linux environment (#310); `internet` — 7 modules against real resolvers and
  servers (#281); **LibL**, the libc face: `fopen`/`fread`/`fwrite`/`fseek`, the remaining `printf`
  formats, `malloc`/`calloc` as spellings over the builtin heap (#397); and **LibC** — link the real
  libc, statically (#415) and at run time (#574). `loment run` calls zlib's `compress`/`uncompress`
  either way (#359, #360). The 0.1.4.5 lock on `use libl` and on libc is open (#406).
- **LMS level 1** — a second memory architecture beside the collector: its checker (E028/E029) and its
  level-3 entry, in both implementations (#414).
- **Potato v14** — `net_ladder`, the width composition of a unit's networking sites (#278); and the
  zero-width phase's static rule (#311).
- **A gate that can see the runtime.** The 104 criteria that need a produced binary now run natively
  on the Linux runner instead of skipping (#380, #382); a criterion that did not run no longer counts
  as a pass, and `.github/gate-floors.txt` is a two-way ratchet (#404). Whole-tree generated artifacts
  left the pull-request path (#447).
- **Distribution.** Read-only mirrors on GitLab, Gitee, Codeberg and Bitbucket, pushed on every commit
  to `main` (#575); a Simplified Chinese README (#573); the VS Code extension is on the Marketplace
  (#273, #274, #275); releases announce themselves to Mastodon (#317, #318).

## fix

- **Reclamation.** The sweeper no longer clears four mark bytes per freed block, which had been
  collecting live blocks next to garbage (#363, #312); `free` checks ownership and refuses a double
  free (#276); block-interior precision landed as per-site slot masks (#315, #286); an argument to a
  whitelisted syscall counts as a borrow, lifting the measured proof surface from 4/23 to 8/23 (#384);
  a collection no longer empties the free list (#407, #366); the collection trigger is attached where
  the bytes are asked for and counts what the allocator consumes, so `str_concat` counts too (#408,
  #412, #367); a recycled block keeps its recorded size, so the walks cannot be derailed (#410, #368);
  a promoted buffer's words reach the root scan (#410, #362); L2's epoch stops at the next same-name
  `let`, so two sibling loops no longer block each other (#585, #364).
- **Diagnostics that used to be silent or wrong.** `@` at statement start, binary literals and the
  fall-off-the-end rule are rejected the way the reference rejects them (#396, #645, #49, #12, #22);
  an unknown type is E030 rather than E002 (#448); seven cases that were silent, wrong or fatal now
  say what the reference says (#398); the same program computes the same numbers in every surface
  grammar (#644, #237); `use std` no longer crashes (#644); the formatter keeps comments and keeps
  declaration modifiers on the declaration's line (#644, #45, #46).
- **The emitter refuses what it cannot express.** Mixed-width arithmetic is a checker error instead of
  invalid IR (#540, #289); `bool != bool` gets the reference's type in the self-hosted compiler (#540,
  #316); 11+ parameters (#540, #265); a struct whose last field has no trailing comma (#540, #11);
  integer literals wrap to their declared type (#535, #529).
- **Runtime and CLI.** Array indexing and arithmetic are checked, division by zero is a trap with a
  message, and the default tier's refusal names the right setting (#533, #18, #19, #321); `let x = 1;`
  (#7), `let a: f64` (#323), a bare `return;` (#335), the compiler's own heap for `brk` (#345), the
  250-term expression (#226) and 400 nested blocks (#44) are diagnosed instead of crashing; Windows
  builds a PE rather than an ELF (#320); `loment check` no longer exits 0 for a file that cannot be
  built (#48); the language server reports the symbol's range (#508, #27, #28) and respects
  `choose write grammar` (#262); user-facing failures stop leaking internal names and unshipped doc
  paths (#440, #8); the Rust backend refuses `free` instead of lowering it to a no-op (#413, #165).
- **Linker.** A negative index is sign-extended (#430, #313); the mirror linker reads 64-bit globals
  and multi-line case tables (#439).
